mappings.note: Content matches the title/introductory doxology of Psalm 68. Order differs slightly (Psaume... vs Til korlederen...) but semantic content is identical.
Includes 'Sela' at the end in both.
Translation uses 'You who lie down...' (plural) while OSMAIN uses 'Even if you rest...' (conditional), but the imagery of silver wings and gold feathers is identical.

Translation says 'Sinaï er i helligdommen' (Sinai is in the sanctuary) or similar phrasing implying location. OSMAIN v18 ends with 'fra Sinai til helligdommen' (from Sinai to the sanctuary). The translation omits the directional movement 'from... to'. However, looking closely at French: 'Sinaï est dans le sanctuaire' vs Norwegian 'fra Sinai til helligdommen'. This is a significant semantic shift/omission. It matches the content of v18 but misses the specific prepositional phrase indicating movement.
Translation says 'harpe' (harp) while OSMAIN says 'strengespillerne' (string players). Semantically equivalent in this context.

Translation: 'Benjamin le petit, le dominateur' (Benjamin the little one, the ruler). OSMAIN: 'den yngste, som leder dem' (the youngest, who leads them). The translation adds 'le dominateur' which is not explicitly in the Norwegian text provided ('som leder dem'). However, 'dominateur' might be an interpretive addition or a slight expansion. Let's look closer. OSMAIN: 'Benjamin, den yngste, som leder dem'. French: 'Benjamin le petit, le dominateur'. The word 'dominateur' (ruler/dominator) is not in the Norwegian text provided. It seems to be an interpretive gloss or extra content.

Translation: 'Il disperse les peuples qui se plaisent aux combats' (He scatters the peoples who delight in war). OSMAIN v31 ends with 'Spre folkene som har lyst til krig!' (Scatter the peoples who desire war!). The translation adds a subject 'Il' (He) and changes the imperative to indicative? Wait, French v31: 'Tance la bête... Il disperse les peuples...' The OSMAIN text is all imperatives: 'Trugg dyret... Tramp dem ned... Spre folkene...'. The French translation splits the last clause into a statement of fact ('He scatters') rather than an imperative ('Scatter'). This is a grammatical shift, but content-wise it matches v31. However, looking at the structure, OSMAIN v31 has three imperatives. French v31 has two imperatives and one indicative statement. The content 'peoples who delight in war' matches.

Translation: 'A celui qui s'avance porté sur les cieux des cieux, les cieux éternels!' (To him who rides on the heavens of heavens, the eternal heavens!). OSMAIN v34: 'Syng for ham som rir på de eldgamle himlers himmel!' (Sing to him who rides on the heaven of ancient heavens). The French adds 'les cieux éternels' (the eternal heavens) as an appositive or expansion not present in the Norwegian text.

Translation v35: 'Rendez la force à Dieu! Sa majesté est sur Israël, sa force est dans les nues.' (Give strength to God! His majesty is over Israel, his strength is in the clouds). OSMAIN v35 starts with 'Gi Gud ære!' (Give God glory!). The translation says 'Give God STRENGTH' ('Rendez la force'). This is a significant content difference. Also, OSMAIN continues: 'Hans majestet er over Israel, og hans makt er i skyene. Fryktinngytende er du, Gud, fra din helligdom! Israels Gud, han gir folket kraft og styrke. Lovet være Gud!' The French v35 stops after 'dans les nues'. The rest of the OSMAIN verse (Fearful are you... He gives strength... Praise God) is missing from French v35.

Translation v36 contains the remainder of OSMAIN v35: 'De tes sanctuaires, ô Dieu, tu te montres redoutable. C'est lui, le Dieu d'Israël, qui donne force et puissance au peuple. Béni soit Dieu!' (From your sanctuaries... you show yourself terrible... He gives strength and power to the people. Blessed be God!). This corresponds exactly to the second half of OSMAIN v35.

extraContent.description: The phrase 'le dominateur' (the ruler/dominator) appears in French but is not present in the Norwegian text ('som leder dem' - who leads them). While semantically similar, it is an explicit addition.
The phrase 'les cieux éternels' (the eternal heavens) is added to the description of the heavens in French, whereas Norwegian only says 'de eldgamle himlers himmel' (heaven of ancient heavens).

The imperative 'Rendez la force à Dieu!' (Give strength to God) differs from OSMAIN's 'Gi Gud ære!' (Give God glory). Additionally, the French v35 omits the final clauses of OSMAIN v35 ('Fryktinngytende er du... Lovet være Gud!'), which are moved to v36.
